definitions.text: A new product or process involving an inventive step and capable of industrial application.
A substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in the aggregation of the properties of the components thereof, or process for producing such substances, is not an invention.
An invention which, in effect, is traditional knowledge or which is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known component or components, is not an invention.
Knowledge derived from authoritative books specified in the First Schedule to the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

productPatent.label: Product Patent
productPatent.whenRecommended: The active compound or composition itself is genuinely novel and not disclosed in TKDL or classical texts.
evidenceNeeded: Structural characterization of the active compound
Comparative novelty search against TKDL and patent databases
Safety and efficacy data per the New Drugs and Clinical Trial Rules, 2019

processPatent.label: Process Patent
processPatent.whenRecommended: The compound itself is already known, but the extraction or manufacturing method is new and non-obvious.
evidenceNeeded: Comparative yield/purity data vs. known methods
Demonstration that the method is not a routine optimization a skilled person would arrive at

design.label: Design Registration
design.whenRecommended: The novelty is in shape, configuration, or visual appearance (e.g. packaging), not the formulation itself.
evidenceNeeded: Statement of novelty distinguishing it from prior designs

tradeSecret.label: Trade Secret
tradeSecret.whenRecommended: The applicant does not wish to publicly disclose the method at all, or the invention is unlikely to clear Section 3(p)/3(e).
evidenceNeeded: Internal documentation of the confidential process
Consider a Prior-Possession Timestamp Certificate as a defensive record
